extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or researchers learning algebraic topology (Steenrod operations, Thom classes, CW complexes)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and propositions about Thom classes, construction and properties of Steenrod powers (P_i), Bockstein interactions and Adem relations, followed by an appendix giving definitions, basic properties, and point-set topology facts about CW complexes and products. Useful for learners working through a graduate-level algebraic topology course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thom class for E1 via CP^{m+1}
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thom space T(E1) is homeomorphic to CP^{m+1}; under this homeomorphism a generator γ ∈ H^2(CP^{m+1}) is a Thom class for E1, restricting to a generator of H^2(S^2_v) on each fiber S^2_v. Choose γ to be the Z_p reduction of an integral generator, determined up to sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret T(E1) as CP^{m+1} by identifying the one-point compactifications of fibers with CP^1's inside CP^{m+1}. The choice of γ is canonical up to sign; use Z_p reduction when working mod p coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: View of Thom classes as relative/cohomology classes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a bundle E→Lp, H^*(T(E)) ≈ H^*(T(E),∞) ≈ H^*(T(E),T(E)−Lp) ≈ H^*(E,E−Lp), so a Thom class may be regarded as an element of H^*(E,E−Lp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use excision and the one-point compactification identification to move between Thom class viewpoints; this is useful when pulling back/pushing forward Thom classes in fiberwise arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of Thom classes via fiber projections
rubrics_metrics.description: If π_j : E→E_j are the fiber projections and τ_j ∈ H^*(E_j,E_j−Lp) are Thom classes, then π_j^*(τ_j) ∈ H^*(E,E−Lp) is a Thom class for E (calculated fiberwise as in Example 3.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce Thom classes on a total bundle, pull back Thom classes from factor bundles via the projection maps; verify by checking restriction to each fiber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Euler-type classes (ej) via maps on Thom classes
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute classes ej coming from the images of Thom classes, follow the class across a diagram: the image of the Thom class for E1 in H^2(CP^m) is the generator γ; f^* multiplies by degree j on CP^1 and q^*(γ)=±ω^2, hence ej = ±j ω^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply degree computations on CP^1 inclusions and identify images under maps like q to get explicit coefficients (signs determined by orientations); track how classes restrict to cells/fibers in the relevant CW-structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Steenrod powers P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: For α ∈ H^n(X), define P_i(α) = (−1)^i a_n^{−1} θ_{2i(p−1)}(α), where a_n ∈ Z_p^× (multiplicative inverse exists) and the sign and normalization are chosen so that P_0 is the identity and P_i(α)=α^p when |α|=2i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the normalizing factor a_n (computed earlier via Thom class pullbacks) so that P_0 = id; include (−1)^i to get the expected behavior on even-degree generators. Verify P_i vanish when 2i > |α|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic properties of P_i operations (naturality, vanishing, Cartan, suspension, additivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The P_i satisfy: naturality; P_i(α)=0 if 2i>|α|; the Cartan formula for products; invariance under suspension; additivity. These properties are inherited from the θ_i operations and established algebraically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking properties for P_i, reduce to analogous facts for θ_i and use the normalization factors a_n consistently. Use the Cartan formula derivation shown to expand P_i on cup products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and number-theory sign fact for P_i
rubrics_metrics.description: The normalization factor a_n must satisfy certain congruences so that P_i behaves as desired on degree-2i classes; a number theory identity (!^2 ≡ (−1)^{(p+1)/2} mod p and factorial congruences) is used to verify a_{2i} = (−1)^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Wilson-type or factorial congruences mod p and parity arguments to compute the needed signs for a_n; these underlie the property P_i(α)=α^p when |α|=2i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bockstein relation with θ-operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma: β θ_{2k} = − θ_{2k+1}. In particular β θ_{2k+1} = 0. This relation follows by computing β∇^*(λ(ι)) and analyzing coefficients in the tensor product H^*(L_∞) ⊗ H^*(K_n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute β on the expansion of ∇^*(λ(ι)) using known β-action on ω_j, track tensor coefficients, and reduce to showing β∇^*(λ(ι)) = 0 by transfer and covering space arguments (τπ^* multiplication by p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adem relations derivation strategy for Steenrod powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive Adem relations by expanding ∇^2 λ^2(ι) in two ways, using only nonzero θ_i's (θ_{2i(p−1)} and θ_{2i(p−1)+1}), applying symmetry ϕ_{rs} = (−1)^{rs+mnp} ϕ_{sr}, and selecting n,ℓ so binomial coefficients force single-term simplifications, yielding the Adem relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial choices of n and ℓ (large p-adic windows) so most binomial coefficients vanish, isolate terms, and then generalize from the class ι to arbitrary classes as in the p=2 case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a CW complex (three-part construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW complex X is built by (1) starting with a discrete set X^0 of 0-cells; (2) inductively attaching n-cells via maps φ_α : S^{n−1} → X^{n−1} so X^n is the quotient of X^{n−1} ⊔ ⊔_α D^n_α by identifications; (3) equipping X with the weak topology (A ⊂ X open iff A ∩ X^n open in X^n for all n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characteristic maps Φ_α : D^n_α → X whose interior maps homeomorphically onto the cell; in finite-dimensional cases condition (3) is automatic. This is the operative cell-by-cell construction used throughout algebraic topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic maps and topology criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A set A ⊂ X is open iff for each characteristic map Φ_α : D^n_α → X, the preimage Φ_α^{-1}(A) is open in D^n_α. This gives an equivalent description of the CW topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this pullback criterion for practical checks of continuity and openness; it underlies many arguments involving maps defined on CW complexes by specifying behavior on each cell.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcomplex characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: A subcomplex A ⊂ X is a union of cells whose closures in X are contained in A (equivalently: a closed union of cells). Its CW topology agrees with the subspace topology from X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with subcomplexes, note they are closed; finite unions of subcomplexes are subcomplexes; use subcomplex neighborhoods for deformation retractions and Mayer–Vietoris/van Kampen setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact subsets contained in finite subcomplexes (Proposition A.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any compact subspace C of a CW complex X meets only finitely many cells and hence is contained in a finite subcomplex of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when reducing global questions to finite subcomplexes (e.g., checking homotopy-theoretic properties or constructing maps), leveraging compactness to avoid infinite-cell complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-finiteness and weak-topology properties (CW axioms restated)
rubrics_metrics.description: CW complexes satisfy: (1) closure-finiteness (closure of each cell meets only finitely many cells) and (2) weak topology (a set is closed iff it meets the closure of each cell in a closed set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These core properties can be used as an alternative definition (Whitehead style) and are useful in many compactness and local finiteness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead's criterion for CW characteristic maps (Proposition A.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given maps Φ_α : D^n_α → X, they are characteristic maps of a CW structure iff (i) each restricts to a homeomorphism int D^n_α → a cell and these cells are disjoint with union X; (ii) Φ_α(∂D^n_α) meets only finitely many lower-dimensional cells; (iii) a subset is closed iff it meets each cell closure in a closed set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this proposition to verify a proposed cell decomposition is actually a CW decomposition; (iii) is automatic when finitely many cells exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of controlled open neighborhoods N_ε(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ε = {ε_α>0} per cell, construct open neighborhoods N_ε(A) inductively over skeleta: on each cell include an ε_α neighborhood of the preimage of A and a collar (1−ε_α,1]×∂D^n in radial coordinates; the resulting N_ε(A) is open in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use N_ε(A) to produce arbitrarily small neighborhoods with product/collar structure near cell boundaries; choose ε_α uniformly small to separate closed sets or produce deformation retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normality and Hausdorff property of CW complexes (Proposition A.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: CW complexes are normal (hence Hausdorff): given disjoint closed sets A and B, choose ε_α small so that the constructed neighborhoods N_ε(A) and N_ε(B) are disjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate closed sets by shrinking the ε_α neighborhoods cellwise; compactness arguments on cell boundaries yield positive distances that allow separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local contractibility and local path-connectedness (Proposition A.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each point in a CW complex has arbitrarily small contractible open neighborhoods (constructed as N_ε(x)), so CW complexes are locally contractible and therefore locally path-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build deformation retractions of N_ε(x) onto lower skeleta by sliding along radial segments in cells; use this to justify local homotopy arguments and standard topological properties used in algebraic topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighborhood deformation retraction for subcomplexes (Proposition A.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a subcomplex A of X, the neighborhood N_ε(A) deformation retracts onto A provided ε_α < 1 for all α: in each cell of X−A the neighborhood is a product of a boundary collar and retracts by the same radial sliding construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is the basis for excision-type arguments and constructing Mayer–Vietoris and van Kampen decompositions using subcomplex neighborhoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact generation and continuity of cellwise homotopies
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW complex X is compactly generated (generated by finite subcomplexes or compact subsets); a map or homotopy from X is continuous iff its restrictions to the closures of cells (or to finite subcomplexes) are continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check continuity of a homotopy, verify it on e^n_α × I for each cell; this relies on X×I being compactly generated when X is a CW complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product CW-structure and product-topology conditions (Theorem A.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural CW structure on (X×Y)_c (the compactly generated product) with characteristic maps the products of cell characteristic maps. If either factor is locally compact (or both have countably many cells), (X×Y)_c equals the usual product topology X×Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing cell structures on products, work in the compactly generated setting. To guarantee equality with the product topology, assume one factor locally compact or both countable-cell; otherwise pathological differences can occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dowker-type example caution (product vs CW topology)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one factor has uncountably many cells, the CW topology on X×Y can be strictly finer than the product topology (Dowker example: uncountably many wedge-intervals vs countably many wedge-intervals producing a closed set in CW topology that is not closed in product topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious when interchanging product and CW topologies in constructions; check countability/local-compactness hypotheses to avoid subtle counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: ENR criterion for compact sets in Euclidean space (Theorem A.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A compact subspace K ⊂ R^n is a retract of some neighborhood iff K is locally contractible in the weak sense: for each x ∈ K and each neighborhood U of x in K there exists V⊂U with the inclusion V→U nullhomotopic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The constructive proof builds a CW decomposition of the complement with cell-sizes shrinking to K, then constructs a subcomplex Z and a map r: Z→K extending to a retraction on a neighborhood; use this to recognize Euclidean Neighborhood Retracts (ENRs).
